clue.text: A firm that's broke can't afford to do it

definitions.text: A firm that's broke can't afford to do it

parts.words: A firm that's broke can't afford to do it
parts.note: an insolvent business stops settling its bills; the clue describes the act it is forced into

explanation.surface: A bankrupt company is unable to pay for something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a firm too poor to buy something; the cryptic sense is the formal halt in settling debts that a broke firm must announce.
explanation.definitionFit: A firm that is insolvent formally halts all settlement of its debts, which is what this phrase names.

clue.text: Dubious character

parts.note: a shady person whom others distrust, such as one the police have in mind for a crime

explanation.walkthrough: The answer works as both adjective (doubtful) and noun (a person under suspicion), and the clue's two words reflect both.
explanation.definitionFit: A person under suspicion, distrusted by police or neighbours, is exactly a dubious character.

clue.text: Live round that's no good

indicators.note: turning a word round shuffles its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A live bullet that turns out to be a dud.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Live round' looks like ammunition; 'round' is the anagram signal that rearranges LIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Something wicked or wrong is morally bad, the opposite of good.

clue.text: Content to go along with 16, 1 apparently

definitions.text: Content to go along with 16, 1 apparently

parts.words: Content to go along with 16, 1 apparently
parts.note: 16 across names a flowing watercourse; someone happy to go along with it lets the current carry them without effort

explanation.surface: Someone happy to follow the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: 16 across is STREAM: to be content to go with the stream is to let oneself be carried along aimlessly. The stray '1' looks like an OCR artefact and does no job.
explanation.definitionFit: Being carried by a current without steering, or living without purpose, is the meaning of the word.

clue.text: Capricious yarn from Turkey P

parts.note: capricious here means goat-derived (Latin capra, goat): soft wool from a Turkish goat named after Ankara

explanation.surface: A tale of whims told in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capricious' looks like 'fickle' and 'yarn' like a story, but the clue means wool from a goat (Latin capra) bred around Ankara. The trailing 'P' is an OCR stray.
explanation.definitionFit: The long silky wool spun from the Ankara goat is a yarn originating in Turkey.

clue.text: Captain Phillips and Mr Benn describing an important figure in Roman history

definitions.text: an important figure in Roman history

parts.note: Captain Mark Phillips, the Olympic horseman once married to Princess Anne
'an' is an old dialect spelling of 'and', as in the contraction an'
Tony Benn, the veteran Labour politician

explanation.surface: Two well-known Britons are pictured as portraying a Roman.
explanation.walkthrough: Captain Mark Phillips was Princess Anne's first husband; Tony Benn was a prominent Labour MP. 'describing' only links the pieces to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesar's general, Cleopatra's lover and a triumvir, he was a leading player in the late Roman Republic.

clue.text: Kind of civet found in West Africa and in 9

annotationWithheld.why: 'Kind of civet found in West Africa and in 9' (7): 'and in 9' gives no wordplay for NANDINE as held; the clue looks garbled by OCR and no source gives its text
annotationWithheld.clue: Kind of civet found in West Africa and in 9

clue.text: Drug-crazy individual keen on being a racing motorist

definitions.text: Drug-crazy individual keen on being a racing motorist

parts.words: Drug-crazy individual keen on being a racing motorist
parts.note: speed is slang for amphetamine, so a person mad about the drug, or a driver obsessed with going fast

explanation.surface: An addict who wants to drive in races.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Speed' is slang for amphetamine, so a person crazy for the drug fits one reading; the other is a driver addicted to going fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone obsessed with going fast, or one hooked on amphetamine, is described by the phrase.

clue.text: In a bound I am filled with ambition

indicators.note: the clue's opening word puts the single letter inside the leap that follows

parts.note: a bound is a leap, a spring

explanation.walkthrough: 'In a bound I' says I goes inside A SPRING; 'am' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone striving to rise or achieve is ambitious, keen to get on.

clue.text: Hastily made approach to the wicket?

definitions.meaning: to sew or knock something together quickly
in cricket, the bowler's run before delivering the ball

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the bowler runs toward the wicket before bowling; that approach is the second sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A tailor may quickly sew up a garment, and in cricket the bowler's charge toward the batsman before releasing the ball has the same name.

clue.text: Tugboats fitted with high level tanks?

definitions.meaning: vessels that tow on the water
raised reservoirs feeding a water supply

explanation.walkthrough: Read the first sense as water + towers: tugs are things that tow on water.
explanation.definitionFit: Tugs haul ships across water, and raised reservoirs on stilts supply mains pressure, so both share the name.

clue.text: In the forenoon he may be said to draw attention

indicators.note: the opening word places the pronoun inside the morning abbreviation

parts.note: AM, ante meridiem, is the morning

explanation.surface: In the morning a man may speak up to be noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'may be' links the wordplay to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A little throat-clearing cough is uttered to get someone's notice.

clue.text: Begin to make light of things

definitions.text: Begin to make light of things

parts.words: Begin to make light of things
parts.note: read as kindling a blaze: setting things alight so that they give off light

explanation.walkthrough: 'make light of' looks like trivialising; read literally it means setting things burning.
explanation.definitionFit: Kindling flames, igniting a blaze, makes light from fuel.

clue.text: A gnome sent all over the a the place for tropical fruit

indicators.note: scattered all over, so the letters are strewn into a new order

explanation.surface: A garden gnome dispatched everywhere in search of exotic fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR text 'all over the a the place' is 'all over the place', the anagram signal; A GNOME SENT is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A purple-skinned Southeast Asian fruit with white segments is a tropical fruit.

clue.text: Boards at a station

parts.note: gets on a railway carriage at a stop

explanation.walkthrough: 'Boards' might be planks or notice-boards; here it is a verb meaning climbs aboard.
explanation.definitionFit: To get onto a railway carriage is to board it at a station.

clue.text: It runs a little way with quite a lot of paper

parts.note: ST is the short form of street, a little way being a small road
a ream is 500 sheets of paper

explanation.surface: A short road and a big pile of stationery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' joins the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A brook or small river flows, i.e. runs.

clue.text: Smokes from Guevara's homeland.

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine revolutionary
one's roots are one's place of origin

explanation.surface: Cigars from the land of the revolutionary.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from' links; the surface hints at Cuban cigars.
explanation.definitionFit: Cigars cut square at both ends are things one smokes.

clue.text: Not far from Trinidad but many miles from Bogota?

indicators.note: being far removed from the capital's name, the letters are moved far from their order

explanation.surface: A Caribbean island near Trinidad but distant from Colombia's capital.
explanation.walkthrough: The island's letters are exactly those of Bogota, the Colombian capital, which is far away; the question mark flags the unusual anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Caribbean island paired with Trinidad in one nation lies just off its coast.

clue.text: Surly mood of market ex-of pecting a fall in prices

definitions.text: mood of market ex-of pecting a fall in prices
definitions.meaning: on the stock exchange, pessimism that share prices will drop

explanation.walkthrough: 'ex-of pecting' is OCR garble for 'expecting'. On the stock exchange, bears sell expecting falls.
explanation.definitionFit: A grumpy person is like a bear, and a market expecting prices to drop is called that, the opposite of bullish.

clue.text: Oriental ball of sinister origin?

definitions.meaning: a dated and now offensive word for a Chinese man
in cricket, a left-arm wrist-spinner's delivery; sinister means left-handed in Latin

explanation.walkthrough: 'sinister' is Latin for left: the ball comes from a left-handed bowler, not from anything evil.
explanation.definitionFit: The first sense is a dated, offensive term for a man from China; the second is a cricket delivery by a left-arm wrist spinner.

clue.text: Italian who won fame by to sending impulsive messages

definitions.text: Italian who won fame by to sending impulsive messages

parts.words: Italian who won fame by to sending impulsive messages
parts.note: the Italian radio pioneer who sent electrical impulses through the air; 'impulsive' looks like rash

explanation.surface: An Italian famed for rash texts.
explanation.walkthrough: 'impulsive' means sent as electrical impulses, i.e. by wireless; the stray 'to' is OCR noise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bologna-born inventor became famous for transmitting the first long-distance radio signals.

clue.text: Small piece of gold found in a clump of elms

indicators.note: the metal is discovered inside the jumbled trees
a clump of trees jumbles them together, so the letters are mixed

parts.note: OR is gold in heraldry

explanation.surface: Bits of gold discovered in a stand of trees.
explanation.walkthrough: The printed 'pieces' is an OCR slip for 'piece', which matches the singular answer. 'a clump of' trees looks like scenery but signals a jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A morsel is a tiny bit, especially of food.

clue.text: Friendly question often raised at the bar

definitions.text: Friendly question often raised at the bar

parts.words: Friendly question often raised at the bar
parts.note: a pub regular offering to buy someone a drink asks this

explanation.surface: A matey enquiry often heard in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the bar' could be the law courts; it is the pub counter where one offers to buy a round.
explanation.definitionFit: Asking a companion which drink they would like is the classic offer to buy a round.

clue.text: A period return for a particular region

indicators.note: a return trip goes back, so the word for period is read backwards

parts.note: an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A return journey to a certain place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A period' tempts as one unit; the A is separate and goes at the end, after the turned-round era.
explanation.definitionFit: A zone or district is a stretch of territory.

clue.text: Mightily impressive Greek character in the City?

indicators.note: the letter sits inside the City's postal code

parts.note: EC, the postcode of the City of London
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: An impressive Greek figure in London's financial district.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Greek character' looks like a hero; it is a letter. EC is the postal district of the City of London, its financial centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand on a heroic scale, as in a heroic poem, is mightily impressive.

clue.text: The EEC's most important currency

parts.note: currency read as current, the flow of water: the leading river of the old European Economic Community

explanation.walkthrough: 'currency' looks like money; read it as 'current', the flow of a river, and the EEC's busiest river is meant.
explanation.definitionFit: Western Europe's chief commercial waterway flows through Germany and the Netherlands, both early members of the community.

clue.text: Highlights a creature with a sting in its tail

annotationWithheld.why: 'Highlights a creature with a sting in its tail' (8): 'a creature with a sting in its tail' defines SCORPION, but 'Highlights' does no job in any parse; the clue looks garbled by OCR
annotationWithheld.clue: Highlights a creature with a sting in its tail

clue.text: How sharper than a serpent's tooth it is To have a "("King Lear", Act 1)

definitions.text: How sharper than a serpent's tooth it is To have a "("King Lear", Act 1)

parts.words: How sharper than a serpent's tooth it is To have a "("King Lear", Act 1)
parts.note: Lear's curse on his ungrateful daughter Goneril; fill in the missing words of the quotation

explanation.walkthrough: A fill-in-the-blank quotation: Lear, cursing Goneril, says ingratitude from one's own child stings worse than a snake.
explanation.definitionFit: Lear laments that an ungrateful offspring wounds a parent more sharply than a snake's bite.
